text: In 1902, people in Hanoi were cutting the tails off live rats... and letting them go. Because the city was paying for tails.
This video is about one strange rule. Every time someone pays for a number... people find the cheapest way to make the number.

Not the thing you wanted. Just the number. We'll see it with rats, with vacuum cleaners, with chocolate pudding, with one of the biggest banks in America, and with the traffic of a whole city. And once — with emus — where paying people actually worked.
